chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halaby, who said:
The woman divorced by Khul'a is not to be provided for.

key_terms.الْمُخْتَلِعَةُ: The woman who gives something to her husband to obtain a divorce (Khul'a)
key_terms.تُمَتَّعُ: To be provided for / given maintenance (mut'ah) upon divorce

ai.seo_question: Is a woman entitled to financial provision if she initiates Khul'a?
ai.summary: This concise hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that a woman undergoing Khul'a (divorce initiated by her, often in exchange for financial compensation) is not entitled to the discretionary gift of maintenance (mut'ah) typically granted to women in standard divorces. This ruling highlights the distinct legal status of Khul'a in Shia jurisprudence, distinguishing it from Talaq based on the principle that the wife's initiation of the separation waives her right to this specific benevolent provision. The brevity of the narration underscores the clarity of the ruling among early Shia scholars regarding the financial implications of mutual or wife-initiated divorce.
